html:
SMTO-POL-0020 — This task ran out of time and was paused

GUID: 85fd43ad-045f-4b08-a95d-1a24689f3bb2
Slug: task-wall-budget-exhausted
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The task reached the time limit it was given, so SMTO paused it. Its progress is saved, but jobs it had already started may still be running in the background.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the paused task and look at its tool calls to see what finished and which background jobs may still be running. Jobs started before the pause can keep working and finish later.
  2. Check the files or computers the task was changing to confirm what is actually done. This stops you asking for the same change twice.
  3. Select Resume on the task to continue it with a fresh time allowance. Resuming carries on the same task from its saved progress instead of starting over.
  4. If you'd rather not continue the whole task, send a new message asking for just the remaining work. A smaller request is more likely to finish within the time it's given.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as running again and then completes, without repeating finished steps.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If the task pauses again, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the whole task again from scratch; finished changes would be made twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run's wall-clock deadline passed at a budget check (budget.wall_clock), so the run was set to paused_budget with work partial; jobs it had already started may still be active.

What this means

  • The task wall-clock deadline has elapsed at budget checking; pausing further work does not establish that already started jobs are inactive. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The task wall-clock deadline has elapsed at budget checking; pausing further work does not establish that already started jobs are inactive.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the saved wall deadline, current task state and active-job receipts before planning a continuation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's completed receipts and any active background jobs before continuing (llm/budget.py InferenceBudget.check, native/run_lifecycle.py prepare_turn). Resume renews the wall budget on the same run from wall_limit_seconds (or a supplied wall_seconds up to 86400); alternatively start a smaller new request. Do not replay prior mutations or disable budget.wall_clock.
  • Inspect completed work and pending effects, then use supported continuation controls or start a smaller new task grounded in the retained results. Do not replay prior mutations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported continuation has a valid lifetime allowance and carries forward the original work evidence without duplicate execution.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the guard as a routine remedy.
  • Do not substitute a different timeout, permission or model setting for this control.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
